title: Dark-launch lanes and acceptance gate playbook for late-binding dependencies
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Quarterly cutovers routinely fail acceptance when late-binding dependencies (infra, security approvals, third-party integrations) land after feature cutover. This causes rolled-back releases, extra engineering cycles, and customer-visible flakiness.

Proposal: Create a playbook and lightweight orchestration layer that: (1) defines 'dark-launch lanes' (traffic-less feature rollout paths) for features with unresolved dependencies, (2) codifies acceptance gates per dependency type (infra, security, design sign-off), and (3) provides automated reminders/escalations and a visible buffer ledger for release managers.

Scope: Playbook + templates + integration with Console rollout UI + runbook for PMs/Release Eng. Includes security gating checklist and a small API to mark dependency status.

Non-goals: Building complex workflow engine or changing existing release pipeline tooling. We will integrate via webhooks and tagging rather than full orchestration in v1.

Trade-offs considered:
- Full workflow engine vs. lightweight lane tagging: chose lightweight to reduce time-to-value and avoid duplicating infra work.
- Strict blocking vs. configurable soft gates: default to soft gates with automatic escalation to minimize developer friction but allow hard blocking for high-risk security dependencies.

Success metrics: % of releases using dark-launch lanes, reduction in rollback rate for Q1 cutovers (target -30%), time-to-approve for security dependencies (target <48h).
acceptance_criteria: Playbook doc in Confluence created with step-by-step lane setup and example scenarios
Console rollout UI shows 'dark-launch' toggle and a per-dependency status column
Webhook contract documented and a sample GitHub action that tags PRs with dependency metadata
Security gating checklist exists and security team has approved the acceptance flow
Two pilot features (one infra-heavy, one security-heavy) complete dark-launch pilot and report metrics
